children: Overview
Canada lumber producer's Q3 sales fell 9% from prior qtr on lower shipment volumes
Company posted C$7.0 mln net loss in Q3, reversing profit from previous quarter
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative in Q3 amid weaker demand and elevated duties
Outlook
Company says North American lumber market faces challenging conditions due to high mortgage rates and weak construction
Lumber prices expected to remain volatile amid subdued demand and industry capacity adjustments
Company expects ongoing trade-related challenges from U.S. duties and tariffs to impact profitability
Result Drivers
LOWER SHIPMENTS - Co said lower shipment volumes, offset by higher realized prices, drove sales decline amid elevated duties and tariffs
INVENTORY PROVISION REVERSAL - Smaller reversal of inventory provision increased cost of sales, offsetting benefits from lower shipments
LOWER SG&A COSTS - Co reduced corporate, administrative and IT-related costs, lowering SG&A expenses
